name: deciding a requirement
from: An analysed requirement nobody has taken up, and a change to an accepted one that somebody is about to make quietly because making it is cheaper than raising it.
to: A requirement the firm has taken up at a named tier, or refused; and a change recorded as a new requirement naming what it changes, so the record still shows that the ask moved.
cost: The deciding body's attention, and the goodwill of whoever raised what got refused. Refusing costs more than accepting and is the half that makes the tier worth anything.
